alignments.note: Anarthrous dative name; rule 21's determinerless clause keeps the case preposition *to* with the noun, headed on the name. The *to* governs the whole appositional dative phrase `μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ` and is placed on the word it immediately precedes in the ASV.
Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 51 helper on the noun it determines rather than an article's determiner, headed on the noun.

Anarthrous genitive; adjective and noun are both anarthrous, so rule 58 gives the supplied determiner *a* to the noun, and the genitive's case preposition *of* rides with it under rule 21. Rule 15 permits the discontinuity across *new*; rule 17 heads on the noun.
Attributive adjective to *new*; rule 58 keeps the supplied determiner on the noun rather than on the adjective standing next to it.
Anarthrous dative noun; the supplied *the* is a rule 51 helper on the noun and the case preposition *to* rides with it under rule 21.
Genitive noun rendered *of + noun*; rule 17 heads on the noun.

Anarthrous participle recast as a finite relative clause; the supplied relativizer *that* is the participle's own helper under rules 7 and 31, headed on the lexical verb under rule 17. No article stands here for the relativizer to compete with.
Comparative preposition to *than*; rule 36 keeps the English preposition on the Greek preposition.

Article governing the expressed name `Ἅβελ`, with which it agrees in case and gender; it is not substantival. The ASV recasts the phrase by supplying the anaphoric nominal *that* and *of* in front of the article's own noun, and rule 102 makes both supplied words the article's and heads the unit on the supplied nominal — REV.11.15's `τοῦ κυρίου` → *the kingdom of*, leaving `κυρίου` a bare *Lord*, is the same shape. Rule 17 confirms *that* over *of*. The competing reading marks *that of* `added` under rules 5 and 103 and leaves `τόν` `unrepresented` under rule 23 as an article before a name, on the strength of the ASV's italics on both words and the margin *Or, than Abel*; it was rejected because rule 11 makes those italics evidence rather than a verdict, no other source token competes for the slot the ASV filled, and rule 102's own REV.11.15 nominal likewise resumes a noun already realized earlier in its verse.
Name to a bare *Abel*, as REV.11.15's `κυρίου` → *Lord* is; the supplied *of* in front of it belongs to the article's unit under rule 102.

review_notes: Partition and heads are unchanged: all 13 source and 22 target ids are still partitioned exactly once, every unit is `aligned`, and no unit's token membership or head moved. The correction is to the reasoning recorded in the notes, chiefly s012.

s012 `τόν` was accepted as a substantival article 'resuming *blood*' under rules 22 and 77. That analysis is not available: `τόν` is T-ASM and agrees with the masculine indeclinable `Ἅβελ` it stands before, so it governs an expressed noun and is not substantival, and a substantival reading pointing at neuter `αἷμα` would need a neuter article. The unit is re-based on rule 102, which covers exactly this shape — an article governing an expressed noun taking a nominal the ASV supplies inside its own phrase, headed on the supplied nominal, with the article's own noun left bare (REV.11.15 `τοῦ κυρίου` → *the kingdom of* / *Lord*). Rule 102 yields the same tokens and the same head, so the accepted alignment stands.

The contested question is recorded in the s012 note as rule 16 requires: `that of` is italicized in the ASV (t020*, t021*) and the margin reads *Or, than Abel*, which supports the competing reading of `that of` as `added` under rules 5 and 103 with `τόν` `unrepresented` under rule 23. It was rejected because rule 11 makes the italics evidence rather than a verdict, `τόν` is free — no other source token has been spent on the slot the ASV filled — and rule 102's REV.11.15 precedent gives a supplied anaphoric nominal to a free article even though that nominal likewise resumes a noun already realized in its verse. A reference comparison that reports `τόν` as represented is not a correction.

Two minor citations were tightened. s005 cited rule 23 for an anarthrous dative name where no article stands at all; it now cites rule 21's determinerless clause alone, and records why the shared `to` of the appositional dative pair `μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ` sits on the name. s010 cited rule 31 for an anarthrous participle; the relativizer is a rule 7 helper on the participle either way, and the note now says that no article competes for it.

Rule 12 is untouched: the packet shows no `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` mark on this verse, so rule 97 is not in play and the projection's `τὸν` is taken as given despite the ASV text reading as though the comparison were blood-to-blood.
